# odyssey-084 — new renderings (table rows)

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| Names in 17.204–305 | Ithacus, Neritus, Polyctor, Dolius, Melanthius, Eurymachus, Phemius, Argus (the dog) | same | "Ithakos", "Nēritos", "Dolios" (shipped in odyssey-020 in the Greek-ending form; the Latinised "Dolius" follows the table's Phemius, Eurymachus, Demodocus), "Melantheus" (Μελανθεύς at 212 and Μελάνθιος at 247 are one man, one English name), "Argos" for the dog (kept for the city, and the table's "Argos" is the place) |
| τὸν δ’ αὖτε προσέειπε Μελάνθιος, αἰπόλος αἰγῶν (whole-line reply-formula, 17.247) | "Him then in turn addressed Melanthius, the goatherd of goats:" | "Then Melanthius, the goatherd of the goats, spoke to him in turn:" | "answered" (reserved for ἠμείβετο), "goatherd" alone (drops the pleonasm αἰπόλος αἰγῶν); built on the table's τὸν δ’ αὖτε προσέειπε συβώτης, ὄρχαμος ἀνδρῶν |
| τοὺς δὲ ἰδὼν νείκεσσεν ἔπος τ’ ἔφατ’ ἔκ τ’ ὀνόμαζεν, / ἔκπαγλον καὶ ἀεικές (two-line speech-introduction of abuse, 17.215–216) | "And them seeing, he reviled them and spoke a word and called them by name, / terrifying and unseemly;" | "When he saw them he reviled them, and spoke, calling them by name, in a terrifying and unseemly way;" | "taunted", "insulted"; the adjectives are taken as adverbs in `i`, as they can be; ἔπος τ’ ἔφατ’ ἔκ τ’ ὀνόμαζεν follows the table's rows for that formula, ἔκπαγλος "terrifying" and ἀεικές "unseemly" the table's |
| νεικέω (aorist, 17.215 νείκεσσεν, 17.238 νείκεσ’) | "reviled" | "reviled" | "rebuked" (shipped for the imperative νείκεε in odyssey-032 and used in the table's ὁμοκλή row; the aorists keep the "reviled" of the table's 8.158 row and of odyssey-035 and odyssey-061), "scolded", "abused" |
| αὐτὰρ ὁ χειρὸς ἑλὼν προσέειπε συβώτην (whole-line speech-introduction, 17.263) | "and he, taking him by the hand, addressed the swineherd:" | "and Odysseus took the swineherd by the hand and spoke to him:" | "answered" (reserved for ἠμείβετο), "grasped", "seized" (too strong for χειρὸς ἑλών); προσέειπε keeps "addressed" in `l` |
| μολοβρός (17.219; meaning not known) | "scrounger" | "scrounger" (+ note: meaning not known; 'glutton' and 'scrounger' are ancient guesses) | "vagrant" (reserved for ἀλήτης), "glutton", "tramp", "gutter-rat" (each picks one guess or adds a colour) |
| ἀμέγαρτος (vocative, of a person, 17.219; the table's ἀμέγαρτος of a blast is "unenviable" / "dreadful") | "unenviable" | "luckless" | "wretched" (reserved for δύστηνος), "miserable" (reserved for δειλός), "pitiable" (reserved for οἰκτρός), "poor fool" (taken by κάμμορε); `l` keeps the literal "unenviable" |

| κνίση (17.270) | "the smell of fat" | "the smell of fat" | "the savour of fat", "steam"; follows the shipped "smell of cooking fat" (κνισῆεν δῶμα) |
